test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A typist takes 40 minutes to type 2 pages. How long (in minutes) will he take to type 101 pages?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of typing = 40 minutes ÷ 2 pages = 20 minutes per page.

Total time for 101 pages = 101 × 20 = 2020 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 2020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken for 2 pages = 40 minutes

Total pages to be typed = 101

**Formula Used:**

In direct proportion: (Work₁ / Time₁) = (Work₂ / Time₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bed6b7acc0b8165075b3c3bea82f3a62b48681bd75550ae26df1185ec6e4f13.png] 

By unitary method:

⇒ Time for 2 pages = 40 minutes

⇒ Time for 1 page = 40 ÷ 2

⇒ Time for 1 page = 20 minutes

⇒ Time for 101 pages = 101 × 20

⇒ Time for 101 pages = 2020 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 2020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in direct proportion if an increase in one leads to a proportional increase in the other. Formula: x/y = Constant.

Work and Time

Total Work = Rate × Time. If the rate of work is constant, the time taken is directly proportional to the amount of work.

Unitary Method

A technique where you first find the value of a single unit (1 page) and then multiply to find the value of the required units (101 pages).
